title: function-calling-parse-debug-scratchpad-maya-6
content:
Goal: root-cause intermittent JSON parse failures when using function-calling to return structured order objects from hosted API. This is my scratchpad for repro steps, logs, experiments and hypotheses.

Background:
- Customer TICKET-4321 reports ~5% of messages fail to parse on our end; client sees 'invalid_response' in SDK when trying to decode assistant.function_call.arguments as JSON.
- Behavior: assistant returns a function call with name\"create_order\" and arguments that often look like JSON but fail json.loads(). Failures include trailing commas, unescaped newlines in string fields, and sometimes naked single quotes.

Repro minimal prompt (used for local repro):
"""
System: You are an order assistant.
User: Create an order for user_id 98421 with 2 items: (sku:AMP-01 qty:1), (sku:BATT-9 qty:2).
"""
Function schema sent (python dict / serialized):
{"name": "create_order", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"user_id": {"type": "string"}, "items": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "object", "properties": {"sku": {"type": "string"}, "qty": {"type": "integer"}}}}}, "required": ["user_id", "items"]}",

Observed bad assistant output examples (copied raw from response body):
1) {"name":"create_order","arguments":"{\"user_id\": \"98421\", \"items\": [{\"sku\": \"AMP-01\", \"qty\": 1,}, {\"sku\": \"BATT-9\", \"qty\": 2}]}"}
--> json.loads() raises: JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 57 (char 56) (trailing comma after qty)

2) {"name":"create_order","arguments":"{\"user_id\": \"98421\", \"items\": [{\"sku\": 'AMP-01', \"qty\": 1}, {\"sku\": \"BATT-9\", \"qty\": 2}]}"}
--> parser fails due to single quotes around AMP-01

3) {"name":"create_order","arguments":"{\"user_id\": \"98421\", \"items\": [{\"sku\": \"AMP-01\\nSPECIAL\", \"qty\": 1}, {\"sku\": \"BATT-9\", \"qty\": 2}]}"}
--> unescaped literal newline in string (literal \n inside SKU) leads to decoding issues in some languages/UTF flows when transmitted via our streaming layer.

Local experiments tried:
- Add JSONLint pass on assistant.arguments string before json.loads() -> detects trailing commas but only safe-fix is to attempt tolerant parser.
- Use regex to replace "\",}" with "\"}" and remove trailing commas in arrays/objects -> works for cases with trailing commas but fragile.
- Force assistant to return JSON only by adding: "Return ONLY a JSON object matching the schema, no surrounding narrative." -> reduces frequency but still occasional malformed outputs (~0.5%).
- Increase temperature to 0.0 and max_tokens tight -> no effect on malformed syntax (indicates model isn't hallucinating content, more like formatting variability).
- Try wrapping output with code fence and parsing inside fences -> consistent but breaks function-calling contract (assistant.function_call.arguments must be raw).

Hypotheses:
1) Model occasionally emits JS-style object literals (trailing commas, single quotes) when the token sampler produces punctuation variants. Lowering temperature reduces but doesn't eliminate.
2) Streaming/transport layer may be altering bytes when long strings include unescaped characters (newlines, unicode). Need to inspect streaming frames for escaping.
3) Our templates around schema might be ambiguous; model sometimes prepends/ appends invisible characters (ZERO-WIDTH SPACE) that make parser fail.

Next runs to do (immediate):
- Add instrumentation: capture exact bytes of assistant.function_call.arguments in raw HTTP body (not decoded) for failed cases and successful cases. Compare hex diffs. (OWNER: Maya)
- Add small tolerant JSON sanitizer in SDK that: attempts json.loads(), on failure runs a deterministic cleanup: remove trailing commas, replace single quotes around keys/strings with double quotes when safe, escape newlines. Log sanitized vs raw. (OWNER: Ashwin)
- Create unit test suite with the 3 bad examples above and edge cases (nested trailing commas, unicode, zero-width space). (OWNER: Ryan)
- Try alternative prompt enforcement: include explicit schema examples (good vs bad) and say "If you cannot produce exact JSON, call function 'error_report' with reason string." See if that reduces malformed outputs.

Notes / breadcrumbs:
- Slack thread: eng-serving-runtime thread/abcd1234 has one customer repro (attached sample response).
- PR #678 in runtime adds extra escaping on the streaming layer (linked above) but we saw no change in preliminary canary.
- Linear RL-1234 tracks shipping tolerant parser in SDK.

Open questions:
- Is this strictly model-side formatting noise or interaction with our streaming/control codes? Need raw bytes.
- If model emits single quotes/trailing commas, should we train better schema/formatting prompts or accept and sanitize at SDK boundary?

Quick TODO (short):
- [ ] Capture raw bytes for 50 failed injections (create debug run).
- [ ] Implement sanitizer prototype and run against customer logs.
- [ ] Add tests and gate in CI.
- [ ] If sanitizer covers >99.5% of cases, ship as hotfix; otherwise escalate to model prompts/ops.

Last modified notes: 2025-11-15 09:40 PST - added hypothesis 3 after seeing U+200B in a failing case.
